description: Displayed wearing the false serial 1901 and earlier 752 per Wrecks and Relics Online. The number 1901 belongs to the MiG-15UTI at the Almaza museum. aviationmuseum.eu reads the marking as 1902.

Displayed wearing the false serial 658 per Wrecks and Relics Online. aviationmuseum.eu gives the serial as 5001 which is the photographically confirmed serial of the Almaza MiG-21F-13 so that reading is rejected.

Construction number 61144 and civil registration SU-AVE. Wrecks and Relics Online records it displayed "As 42" but photographs taken by the Egypt Wikimedians User Group on 14 February 2026 show it marked 601 so the display marking has been changed since that compilation was written.
Displayed wearing the false serial 7751 and earlier 803 per Wrecks and Relics Online. The number 7751 belongs to the Su-17K at the Almaza museum.

Wrecks and Relics Online records it displayed "As 46" but a photograph taken by the Egypt Wikimedians User Group on 14 February 2026 shows 151 in Arabic-Indic numerals on the forward fuselage so the marking has been changed. aviationmuseum.eu reports 151 as if it were the serial.

True identity not established. Wrecks and Relics Online records it displayed "As 61" while aviationmuseum.eu reports 201; neither is a confirmed serial so tail_number is left blank. Seen and described at this museum by Richard Seaman.
